Here is the reason why 99.9% of people trying to sell digital products on X stay stuck under $8K/month:

( I normally charge people for this information )

HARSH TRUTH : The problem isn't your content. It's your fundamental misunderstanding of how buyers actually make purchasing decisions online.

When you position yourself as "here's a course that teaches you stuff," you're already losing.

Top X creators making $50K-$100+/month NEVER sell this way.

Instead they position their offer as a MANDATORY SHORTCUT to an outcome the buyer is already desperate for.

Let me cook.

The psychological shift is MASSIVE.

When you say "I'll teach you how to grow and make money," buyers ask themselves "do I need this?" which ALWAYS results in a NO.

But when you say "While you've been figuring this out alone for 6 months, other people in your exact situation just quit their jobs using this exact system and make $15K/mo"

The conversation shifts from "do I need this?" to "how much time have I already wasted?"

And people don't like feeling behind.

They don't need "a course."

They need a guarantee they won't be left behind.

Here's what 99% of people selling digital products fail to understand:

EVERY buyer already has money allocated. They just haven't given it to you yet because you haven't framed your offer correctly.

Their "I can't afford it" budget is a lie.

They spent $200 last month on subscriptions they don't use.

They dropped $500 on something that promised results and delivered nothing.

The money exists. You just haven't become the priority yet.

Your prospect doesn't have a money problem. They have a PRIORITY problem.

Fix that and watch objections disappear.

And keep in mind that most buyers don't make logical decisions about purchases.

They buy based on:

- perceived urgency (FOMO always converts first)
- social proof (if someone like them already won, they need in)
- identity (they buy the version of themselves that succeeds)

But when you show someone exactly how much their current path is costing them in time, money and missed opportunity : they don't "find new money." They REALLOCATE from Netflix, eating out, random Amazon purchases.

Stop selling your program and start selling the cost of inaction:

1 — Find their current bleeding (ex: they've been "figuring out content" for 6 months with zero sales)

2 — Expose the real cost (ex: at even $3K/month you've lost $18K in the last 6 months trying to do this alone)

3 — Redirect that logic to you (ex: for the same $5K you've already wasted on courses that gave you no support, you get a done-for-you system and a team behind you)

Now the buyer sees ZERO new risk. Just a smarter allocation of what they were already spending.

Buyers love this because it makes them feel like they're finally making an intelligent decision.

Most sellers pitch one benefit but you need to sell CHAIN REACTIONS in the buyer's life.

MOMENTUM COMPOUNDS LIKE DOMINOES.

If you can show that investing in one thing will unlock time, income, freedom and identity simultaneously — the buyer has NO CHOICE but to say yes.

$$$

Got it??

result.text:
big in diy here. Agreed that its gonna be cheaper than most big brands that charge 1000% markups. In the case of IKEA, getting the raw materials is more expensive that getting the finished piece, because of economies of scale (sourcing in big vols).
Atm there's a sweet spot of getting the materials and paying a craftsman to follow instructions and it would cost probably 1/10 of the brand to knock it off (if craftsman is skilled).

Most of woodwork will be done by cnc. Due to robotics a lot of other techniques (eg bending, layering, finishing) will also soon be automated. Upholstery will be the last bit. 

In any case, customizability in factories is what a lot of robotics will change
